ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monetaire et financier, Articles L561-1 to L561-57 (anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing obligations for supervised entities); Ordonnance no. 2020-115 du 12 fevrier 2020 (transposition of EU Directive 2015/849 as amended by Directive 2018/843); Decret no. 2016-1897 du 28 decembre 2016 (registre des beneficiaires effectifs, RBE); Decret no. 2021-1321 du 11 octobre 2021 (procedural rules for the RBE filing through the Registre national des entreprises); Code de commerce, Articles L123-1, R123-166 and R123-232-1 (RBE filing requirements); Reglement ACL no. 2021-01 of the ACPR on anti-money laundering for financial intermediaries.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or corporate registry extract of each corporate shareholder, evidencing entity existence and ownership chain for full UBO piercing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the shareholder's home jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Commercial Register, Ministry of Corporate Affairs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin state is a party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise full Consular Legalization at the French Embassy or Consulate of the origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of identity and capacity of each proposed manager (gerant) and authorized signatory, including passport copy and power of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent local authority in the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; certified French translation by a sworn translator (traducteur agree) admitted before the French Cour de cassation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct or extract of criminal records (extrait de casier judiciaire) of each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the manager's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization followed by sworn translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds attestation for each founding shareholder covering proposed initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating credit institution or financial institution holding the shareholder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the notarized signature or bank certification; sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: RBE declaration form (Formulaire d'identification des beneficiaires effectifs) identifying every individual holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of shares or voting rights or controlling the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The founders' representative filing through the INPI Guichet Unique
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal statutory declaration executed before a notary or certified by the representative of the founders; no apostille required for internal forms

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for all founders, managers and beneficial owners including: (i) screening against the French Treasury financial sanctions list (Fonds de gel des avoirs / gels internationaux); (ii) screening against the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; (iii) screening against United Nations Security Council consolidated lists; (iv) risk-based overlay screening against the United States OFAC SDN List and Department of Commerce Entity List; (v) Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification and enhanced monitoring in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12, Articles L561-10 and L561-12 of the Code monetaire et financier and ACPR/AMF inspection doctrine; (vi) continuous transaction monitoring during the post-incorporation lifecycle; and (vii) documentation of beneficial ownership chain through to natural persons whenever corporate shareholders are interposed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique Electronique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operating the Registre national des entreprises (RNE) and coordinating with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be expressed in French or in any foreign language provided it is usable in Latin script in all French legal instruments; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the French alphabet. The name must be distinctive, truthful, not misleading, and compatible with French public policy. Every deed and document issued by the SARL must be headed by the corporate name followed by 'Societe a responsabilite limitee' or 'SARL' and the registered office address, as required by Article L223-18 of the Code de commerce.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France (when implying official French state or public authority affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not provide a statutory pre-filing name reservation; the name is examined by the INPI Guichet Unique during the incorporation filing. If the name is rejected, the applicant receives a motivated refusal notice and may submit curative corrections within 15 days through the same portal. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may file a formal administrative appeal with the INPI and thereafter a judicial recourse before the Tribunal judiciaire de Paris within two months of the final refusal, or petition the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for review of non-registration. Any private-law opposition based on prior trademark or corporate name rights must be pursued before the competent commercial court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible only through a licensed commercial domiciliation agent (societe de domiciliation) authorized by the Prefecture under Article L123-11-1 of the Code de commerce. The domiciliation arrangement must include a real contractual office location in France, professional mail handling, availability during business hours and retention of accounting records at the domiciled address. A purely nominal mailbox with no administrative substance is not acceptable; the DGFiP may reclassify the registered office under Article L64 of the Livre des procedures fiscales and the ACPR or tax authorities may pierce the arrangement for abuse of law if no genuine local management presence is maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium_Risk_Approximately_25_Percent_Annual_Assessment for an ISIC 4690 re-invoicing intermediary with no licensed status; the likelihood increases substantially (up to 60 percent) where the sole local substance is a third-party domiciliation agent and where invoicing volumes are disproportionate to French operational headcount.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory incorporation filing with INPI Guichet Unique and registration in the Registre national des entreprises and Registre du commerce et des societes (greffe fee and state levies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by Decret no. 2016-1060 and the official greffe fee schedule (barème des greffes)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in a legal announcements journal (Journal d'annonces legales / JAL) for the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market price per line regulated by the Prefecture tariff ceiling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the French articles of association (statuts) of the SARL by a licensed French avocat, including share transfer restrictions, manager powers and quorum provisions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard SARL incorporation with diversified shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation of foreign corporate documents, certificates and identity papers by a translator admitted to the French Cour de cassation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-page tariff and prevailing professional benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification or consular legalization of the full UBO piercing document bundle at the competent authority of the origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority or French consular post in the origin jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular fee schedule and apostille administrative tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial office domiciliation agreement with an approved domiciliation agent for the first twelve months, covering receipt of mail, inspection readiness and legal notice posting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for commercial domiciliation with regulatory compliance support in Paris or major commercial center

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory UBO (RBE) declaration preparation and submission, including cascade ownership analysis through intermediate entities and identification of natural person beneficial owners above the 25% threshold
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI Guichet Unique and professional advisor fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official e-filing fee at zero cost; advisory fees at prevailing market benchmark for multi-tier ownership structures

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and international sanctions screening report including French Fonds de gel, EU and UN lists, OFAC SDN overlay and adverse media checks on all shareholders, managers and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed AML/CFT compliance consultant or data provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing subscription and per-subject screening market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the French professional business bank account, including KYC documentation review and source-of-funds verification for the initial share capital deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution or neobank with French IBAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for professional account opening and administrative compliance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for notarial attestation of capital contribution (attestation du depot des fonds) and miscellaneous administrative stamps and courier costs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and administrative service providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and official stamp schedules

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Articles R.223-1 et seq. and R.123-30 et seq. on RCS registration formalities; Decree No. 2009-1085 of 19 August 2009 on business formalities; Order of 28 October 2021 establishing the single business window (guichet unique).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the competent commercial court for the registered office; filing is made electronically through the INPI national single window at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: The unified business-creation declaration (M0 form) combined with the signed statutory articles (statuts) and the supporting deposit and publication certificates, filed through the guichet unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to a French SARL under Article L.223-2 of the Code de commerce; the articles may set the capital at €1 or higher, with €1,000 recommended for this re-invoicing hub. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and at least 20% of each cash portion must be paid up on incorporation, with the balance to be liberated within five years. All cash funds are deposited in a blocked bank account, with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or a notary, and are released to the Manager only upon presentation of the Kbis registration extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST INCORPORATORS' RESOLUTION OF THE SARL — The undersigned associates, acting under Articles L.223-7 and L.223-18 of the French Commercial Code, unanimously resolve: (1) the final articles of association are adopted; (2) the share capital set out therein is subscribed in full and cash contributions have been duly deposited; (3) the registered office is established at the address stated in the articles, effective upon registration in the RCS; (4) the natural person named in the articles is appointed sole Manager (gérant) with the broadest powers for the general re-invoicing and trade intermediary activity; and (5) the Manager is authorized to complete all registration filings before the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Associates jointly; optional certification by a Notaire (notary) of the department of the registered office, e.g., Notaires de Paris for a Parisian seat.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft statutory articles containing the corporate form (SARL), corporate name, corporate object limited to ISIC 4690 wholesale trade intermediation and commercial re-invoicing, registered office address, share capital, manager designation, and share-transfer clauses under Article L.223-13 C. com. Each associate must sign every page with the handwritten formula 'lu et approuvé'. If a notary is engaged, execute an authentic deed (acte authentique); otherwise the statuts remain a private deed.
required_dossiers: Statuts (private deed or notarized authentic deed)
Valid identity documents of each associate
Power of attorney for any proxy signatory
Kbis extract and representative's identity where an associate is a legal person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or the single window identifies a drafting defect, execute an amending agreement (avenant) signed by all associates and re-submit; for notarized deeds, request a rectificatory notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Share-Capital Account and Deposit of Cash Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed French bank of the company's choice or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The future Manager opens a provisional account titled 'SARL [Name] — société en formation' and deposits the cash portion of the subscribed capital. The bank issues an attestation de dépôt de fonds stating the depositor, the beneficiary company, the amount, and the blocking condition. The blocked funds are released to the Manager only upon presentation of the issued Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts
Identity documents of the depositing associates
Provisional account opening and AML/KYC forms
Source-of-funds documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account opening for compliance reasons, deposit the capital with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or an alternative bank; if the attestation contains defects, obtain a corrected attestation from the depositary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Formation Announcement (Avis de Constitution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized in the judicial department of the registered office, e.g., Petites Affiches Parisiennes for a Paris seat.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to the selected JAL a notice containing the corporate form, name, capital, registered office address, corporate object summary, duration, Manager's identity, and the Commercial Court of jurisdiction. The JAL publishes the notice and delivers the attestation de parution, which is a mandatory attachment to the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Data sheet of the announcement
Copy of the draft statuts or a corporate data synthesis
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL requires a correction or clarification, publish an erratum notice at the applicant's cost and obtain an updated attestation de parution before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal Registration Filing through the Single Business Window (Guichet Unique)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) administered by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; all filings are made electronically via the INPI national single window at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0/M1 business-creation declaration on the guichet unique, attach the executed statuts, deposit certificate, publication certificate, beneficial-owner declaration, and the Manager's declaration of no disqualification. Pay the official filing fee (EUR 80.60, approximately USD 87). The greffe performs the legality review, registers the company, and issues the official status; the Kbis extract is then delivered.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 creation declaration on the guichet unique
Statuts signed by all associates
Attestation de dépôt de fonds or notarial deposit certificate
Attestation de parution from the legal announcements journal
Declaration of beneficial owners (bénéficiaires effectifs)
Manager's identity documents and declaration of non-conviction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues a request for supplementary documents, comply within the stated statutory deadline by uploading the missing items on the single window; where the dossier is finally rejected, correct the defects and file a fresh application; a wrongful refusal may be challenged before the presiding judge of the competent commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Deliverables: Kbis Extract, SIREN and Tax Numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; INSEE for statistical identifiers; Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) for VAT; Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects for EORI in third-country trade.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the greffe issues the Kbis extract, which constitutes the official identity certificate of the company. INSEE attributes SIREN and SIRET numbers automatically. The DGFIP activates the intra-Community VAT number for the re-invoicing activity. Where goods are imported from or exported to third countries, the Manager submits a separate EORI application to French Customs.
required_dossiers: Kbis registration acknowledgment
VAT number notification (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire)
EORI application, if third-country customs transactions are planned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is not promptly notified, file a written activation request with the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises; if the Kbis contains typographical or legal errors, apply to the greffe for a rectification order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Governance and Social Registration of the Manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF (social affiliation of the non-salaried Manager); the commercial court greffe for the officers' register; insurance sector for professional civil liability.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Affiliate the sole Manager as a travailleur non salarié (TNS) with URSSAF within eight days of Kbis issuance. Open the corporate governance file comprising the statutory register (registre des décisions), the first minutes, and the managers' mandates. Subscribe to professional civil liability insurance adapted to a cross-border re-invoicing hub and bank-mandated directors' liability cover where required.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract
Manager's identity and residential address
Company bank account details
Executed articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF delays the affiliation, regularize the situation retroactively through the URSSAF portal using the Kbis and the registration acknowledgment; any unjustified refusal of affiliation is remedied by a formal written complaint to the URSSAF director or the social security tribunal.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique — taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; company registration/registry portal: guichet-entreprises.fr / infogreffe.fr; French VAT is administered by DGFiP via the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), with large taxpayers serviced by the Direction des grandes entreprises (DGE); customs and export duties are administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) through the Guichet Unique du Dédouanement (GUN) / operational import-export platform; the national e-invoicing infrastructure is the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF), interoperable with certified Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires (PDPs).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SARL through guichet-entreprises.fr; obtain INSEE SIREN and SIRET numbers, the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) extract (Kbis) and the NAF Rev. 2 activity code matching the ISIC 4690 re-invoicing scope, i.e., 46.90B (other non-specialised wholesale trade). 2. Register the TIN/TVA number: file the commencement of taxable activity declaration (M0/M1) and apply for the intra-Community VAT identification number (numéro d'identification TVA intracommunautaire) in the format FR + 11 digits from the competent DGFiP service; the application is generally processed within one month and the number is evidenced by the 'extrait d'immatriculation TVA'. 3. For a re-invoicing hub buying from non-established suppliers, French VAT applies by reverse charge (art. 283-1 CGI) so the French SARL itself is the taxable debtor and must be VAT-registered from the first taxable transaction; there is no registration threshold for foreign suppliers selling into France unless they elect the importer-of-record or franchise regime. 4. Obtain a customs EORI number (format FR + SIREN) from DGDDI, free of charge, through the Guichet Unique du Dédouanement, to lodge export declarations and customs transit formalities. 5. Register as principal for the e-invoicing reform: subscribe to a certified PDP or use the PPF, and complete technical onboarding before the applicable issuance/reception deadlines (1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises; 1 September 2027 for SMEs/VSEs). 6. Where the SARL acts for foreign principals under a commissionaire or re-invoicing model, appoint responsible officers and maintain SIC (Système d'Information Comptable) and treasury files evidencing that commercial risk, inventory risk and invoicing authority are genuinely held by the SARL; the DGFiP may recharacterise the hub as an artificial interposition if no substance is demonstrated. 7. Foreign traders without French establishment that wish to use the SARL as a strategic re-invoicing vehicle must not merely 'pass through' invoices; they must appoint a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) approved by DGFiP only where the foreign principal itself incurs French VAT liabilities; the SARL's own French VAT number suffices for its independent resell operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — An ordinary commercial SARL incorporated under French law is by default a taxable person subject to l'impôt sur les sociétés (corporate income tax) under art. 206-1 CGI on its worldwide profits derived from French business activity, unless the profits are attributable to a foreign permanent establishment, in which case France's territorial limitation in treaty/domestic law applies only to the foreign PE (art. 209-I CGI). The SARL is also a normal VAT taxable person without the publicity or pass-through attributes of a partnership; it is fully liable for French VAT on its taxable supplies, imports and intra-Community acquisitions, and can recover input VAT in accordance with art. 271 CGI. For ISIC 4690 re-invoicing operations, the SARL is the legal principal in the chain and its taxable margin (resale price minus cost of goods) is subject to French entity-level taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. The available statutory elections and transparency mechanisms for a foreign-owned French SARL engaged in general re-invoicing trade are: (1) family SARL income-tax option under art. 239 bis AA CGI, restricted to qualified family-held companies and therefore generally unavailable for an arms-length commercial re-invoicing hub; (2) tax consolidation election (régime d'intégration fiscale) under art. 223 A CGI for a French group holding at least 95 percent of the SARL's share capital and voting rights, allowing the group to pool French taxable results and offsets; (3) ordinary IS regime versus the reduced IS regime for small and mid-size enterprises when statutory turnover and ownership conditions are met; (4) VAT filing elections, including monthly versus quarterly declarations and the exporter's election for monthly VAT credit refunds (remboursement du crédit de TVA); (5) OSS (Union/Non-Union One Stop Shop) and IOSS elections for distance sales and for imported consignments valued at EUR 150 or less; (6) anti-hybrid and mismatch treatment: France transposed ATAD and ATAD2 into art. 209 and 212 bis CGI, so no elective 'check-the-box' carve-out is recognised; a French SARL cannot be disregarded merely because a foreign affiliate treats it as transparent, and any mismatch that produces double non-taxation or a deduction without corresponding inclusion is neutralised by the French administrative authority; the taxpayer may, however, elect to be treated as a transparent entity only in jurisdictions whose domestic law so provides, and must disclose such mismatches in the annual tax return (file 2257) to avoid the 80 percent abuse-of-right penalty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by articles 256 to 289 of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI) and implementing the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France applies the franchise en base de TVA (small-business exemption) at EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for supplies of services, with tolerance (reduced) thresholds of EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,000 respectively; the exemption is mandatory below those ceilings and cannot be waived, but it does not apply to imports, intra-Community acquisitions, or to taxable persons conducting export, triangulation or distance-selling operations. A wholesale re-invoicing and export hub under ISIC 4690 is therefore required to register for VAT from its first taxable transaction even if its turnover is below the franchise ceilings, because the franchise is excluded for cross-border supplies, goods held on consignment and services connected to exports; the hub should register with the SIE immediately upon incorporation and maintain VAT registration irrespective of the turnover thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing under the French facturation électronique reform (loi de finances 2024/2025; art. 289 CGI): every French-established taxable person must be able to receive structured electronic invoices through a certified PDP or the PPF from 1 September 2026; issuance is phased, with large and mid-size enterprises required to issue via the PPF/PDP from 1 September 2026 and SMEs/VSEs from 1 September 2027. The regime applies to all domestic B2B transactions and to B2C/business-outside-France transactions through e-reporting of transaction data; there is no per-invoice real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping, but each PDP must transmit invoice data to the PPF within one working day, and the PPF maintains a national invoice directory and data monitoring facility. Foreign suppliers subject to French VAT (including OSS/IOSS registrants) must comply with equivalent structured-data reporting for their French supplies. For a re-invoicing hub, the e-invoice must carry the mandatory fields: French TVA number, customer's TVA number (where B2B), VAT breakdown at 20 percent or 0 percent with the appropriate exemption code, and, for exports, the customs declaration references and transport evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 1. Exports of goods outside the European Union (art. 262-I-1° CGI): the supply is entitled to a 0 percent VAT rate if the French seller transfers ownership of the goods, physically dispatches them from French territory (or from a French customs warehouse) to a destination outside the EU, and holds evidence of the export declaration (DAU/EX1) and actual physical exit from the EU within three months from the date of supply; failure to evidence physical exit within that window triggers a retroactive 20 percent VAT assessment. 2. Intra-EU deliveries (art. 262 ter CGI): the supply is exempt with 0 percent output VAT where the customer provides a valid TVA intra-Community identification number and the French hub files the recapitulative statement reporting the sale. 3. Services directly connected to exported goods (art. 262-II CGI), including transport, handling, inspection, insurance and ancillary commission services rendered to a non-EU principal, qualify for the export exemption where the goods are actually exported outside the EU. 4. For pure offshore re-invoicing and intermediary commissions: where the French SARL renders services to a foreign entrepreneur and the place of supply is outside France under art. 259-4 CGI (B2B main rule, customer-established basis), no French VAT is chargeable (outside scope/0 percent equivalent); the hub must maintain a business attestation from the foreign customer confirming its VAT status and business location. 5. Low-value imported consignments (≤ EUR 150) may be sold through the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) without French import VAT, followed by an exempt onward supply; alternative structuring (normal import clearance then domestic sale) triggers import VAT and standard French treatment. 6. A zero-rating claim cannot be based on mere re-invoicing, paper transfers, or triangular invoice flows if the goods never leave the EU or the French hub does not legally act as principal; diversion, re-importation or abandonment of the goods destroys the exemption and invokes the penalty regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation / DAU with EX-status) lodged in the Guichet Unique du Dédouanement and endorsed by DGDDI, with the MRU/out-turn reference
Bill of Lading (Connaissement maritime) or equivalent transport document (Air Waybill / CMR road consignment note) evidencing dispatch from France to a destination outside the EU

Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign payment evidence — SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wire confirmation, or a bank attestation showing receipt of export proceeds in the French hub's account within the contractual payment window
Commercial invoice, underlying purchase order and sales contract establishing legal ownership transfer from the SARL to the foreign customer
Transport and insurance documentation (packing list, weight note, container tracking, insurance certificates) confirming the physical movement of goods out of the European Union
For intra-EU supplies: recapitulative statement (État récapitulatif de TVA) and the customer's validated TVA intra-Community number
Customs or licensed-agent mandates (power of attorney, forwarding instructions, EX1 follow-up certificates) if export clearance is performed by a third-party broker
IOSS/OSS registration references and import VAT evidence when low-value consignments are routed through the Import One-Stop-Shop
Intercompany documentation for related-party re-invoicing, including transfer pricing documentation for commission rates and margin allocation to support the economic substance of the French hub
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: French export zero-rating is subject to joint audit scrutiny by DGFiP (VAT audit) and DGDDI (customs control). If the export declaration, bill of lading, payment evidence or exit proof is missing, inaccurate or fraudulent, the 20 percent VAT is retroactively clawed back, plus interest at 0.20 percent per month (intérêt de retard) under art. 1727 CGI. In cases of bad faith or deliberate concealment, the 40 percent penalty for mauvaise foi applies under art. 1729 CGI; for fraud or abuse of right the penalty rises to 80 percent, and the auditor may apply the fiscal abuse procedure under art. L.64 LPF to disregard artificial re-invoicing arrangements. Customs offences (code des douanes) carry confiscation of goods and a fine ranging from one to five times the tax evaded; criminal tax evasion under art. 1741 CGI exposes the natural-person directors to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, and the SARL itself is subject to civil recovery, denial of export VAT refunds (remboursement du crédit de TVA), forfeiture of the monthly-refund election, publication of sanctions and de-registration from the PPF/PDP ecosystem. The general DGFiP assessment window is three years (art. L.169 LPF), extended to ten years for concealed or fraudulent activity (art. L.176 LPF), and the bank and treasury records (SWIFT confirmations, IBAN statements, FX contracts) supporting the export proceeds must be retained for at least ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, including its Foreign Exchange and Balance of Payments reporting functions; prudential and payment-services supervision is principally conducted by the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, while customs and trade-flow controls are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general foreign-exchange control regime. Current-account payments, including imports, exports, services, interest, dividends, and ordinary commercial settlements, are generally freely transferable. Capital movements, shareholder funding, intercompany loans, acquisitions, and profit distributions are also generally permitted, subject to anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax, corporate-law, beneficial-ownership, and statistical-reporting requirements. A SARL may remit legally distributable profits, interest, and loan principal to non-resident owners or lenders, provided accounts are approved, corporate approvals are documented, withholding-tax and transfer-pricing rules are satisfied, and the bank receives an adequate source-of-funds and purpose file. Certain foreign investments and acquisitions involving sensitive French sectors may require prior notification or authorization under French foreign-investment-control rules. Cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more across the EU external border require customs declaration, and banks may request supporting documentation for unusual cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, convert them into euros, or repatriate them within a prescribed period. Export receipts may remain in foreign-currency accounts or be netted through approved banking arrangements, subject to contractual, accounting, tax, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering controls. Exporters must retain commercial invoices, contracts, transport and customs evidence, payment records, and VAT documentation. Banks may request export evidence before processing or releasing funds, and Banque de France statistical or balance-of-payments reporting may apply to designated transactions or reporting populations. No universal mandatory conversion ratio or statutory export-collection deadline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account for SARL formation, followed by Operational Current Account and Foreign-Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant regional Crédit Agricole caisse
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account, Operational Current Account, Trade Finance Account, and Foreign-Currency Account
Capital Deposit Account, Operational Current Account, Trade Finance Account, and Foreign-Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. and the relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne institution
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit Account, Operational Current Account, and Trade Finance Account
Operational Current Account and Foreign-Currency Account, subject to business-segment acceptance

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection, SEPA transfers, multi-currency wallets, and routine supplier payments; Low as the sole banking architecture for a trade re-invoicing hub requiring capital deposit, documentary trade finance, letters of credit, substantial foreign-currency turnover, or access to cash-management credit. An EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide regulated payment services under its authorization and passporting rights, but it does not provide a bank deposit in the legal sense, may be required to safeguard customer funds rather than maintain them as deposits, and may not offer credit, deposit-taking, documentary letters of credit, or certain treasury products without separate authorization. Offshore digital EMIs without EU authorization, passporting, or an appropriately licensed EU agent should not be used for core operating receipts or material cross-border settlement. The SARL must complete the EMI's legal-entity, UBO, source-of-funds, transaction-profile, sanctions, and expected-volume checks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors attend a bank branch in person. Remote onboarding may be available where the institution supports qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified documents, and acceptable digital-signature procedures. Banks may nevertheless require a physical meeting, original or notarized documents, certified translations, a French-resident contact, or enhanced interviews for foreign-owned entities, newly incorporated SARLs, high-value trade flows, complex ownership chains, non-standard jurisdictions, or elevated transaction volumes. The legal representative, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners must be identified and verified; a bank may suspend onboarding or transactions until the verification is complete.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership chain is opaque, contains nominee shareholders, uses trusts or layered holding companies, or lacks a clearly identifiable natural-person UBO.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current French corporate extract from the Registre national des entreprises, articles of association, shareholder register, complete ownership chart to natural-person UBOs, certificates of incorporation for foreign entities, registers of directors and shareholders, passports and address evidence for UBOs and directors, trust or nominee documentation where applicable, and signed beneficial-ownership certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business model is described as re-invoicing, intermediary trading, or offshore commerce without sufficient commercial substance or clear value creation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business memorandum, product and supplier descriptions, customer and supplier contracts, purchase orders, commercial invoices, logistics and title-transfer model, Incoterms, customs procedures, margin policy, agency or principal analysis, organizational chart, staffing and office evidence, website and marketing materials, and a 12-month transaction forecast by country, currency, counterparty, and payment type.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected flows involve high-value imports or exports, rapid pass-through of funds, third-party payments, unusual payment corridors, or transactions inconsistent with the declared business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury and payment policy, counterparty master file, invoice-to-payment reconciliation process, purchase orders, bills of lading, customs declarations, certificates of origin, proof of delivery, bank statements, source-and-use-of-funds schedule, transaction-monitoring controls, exception-approval matrix, and documented prohibition of unrelated third-party payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctioned countries, sanctioned persons, dual-use goods, restricted commodities, or counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening policy covering EU, UN, French, UK, and relevant U.S. restrictions, counterparty screening records, end-user and end-use certificates, product classification, export-control review, denied-party controls, shipment-route analysis, licenses or authorizations, and written escalation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient evidence for capital injection, shareholder loans, dividend payments, interest, or other cross-border related-party transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolutions, capital subscription documents, bank capital-deposit certificate, executed loan agreement, loan pricing and maturity terms, beneficial-owner source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, repayment schedule, transfer-pricing support, board approval, French accounting entries, tax analysis, and proof of withholding-tax compliance where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, permanent-establishment, VAT, customs, or transfer-pricing inconsistencies between the payment activity and the declared French operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax registration, VAT number, customs EORI registration, tax-residency certificates, VAT and customs process map, intercompany agreements, transfer-pricing policy, master and local files where applicable, permanent-establishment analysis, management-and-control evidence, and filings or correspondence with relevant authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete identity records, expired passports, inconsistent addresses, non-certified translations, or inability of signatories to explain the business and payment flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current identity documents, recent address evidence, specimen signatures, powers of attorney, certified French or English translations, corporate authorization matrix, signatory interview preparation file, and a concise transaction-flow presentation matching the onboarding questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, politically exposed person status, criminal or regulatory history, or unexplained wealth indicators involving a UBO, director, or key counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent adverse-media review, legal and regulatory explanations, court or settlement documents, PEP declaration, enhanced source-of-wealth file, source-of-funds evidence, compliance-office approval, risk-mitigation plan, and senior-management sign-off where required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For SARL formation, subscribe the capital into a French bank's restricted capital-deposit account before registration, using a transfer from an account held by the subscriber or documented investor. The bank should receive the draft articles of association, subscription schedule, identity and UBO documents, corporate approvals, source-of-funds evidence, and intended-use statement. After registration, provide the Kbis extract and use the bank's certificate to release the funds to the operational account. For subsequent equity injections, route funds through SEPA Credit Transfer in euros or SWIFT cross-border payment in the investment currency, clearly identifying the French SARL, investor, amount, currency, and purpose as equity contribution or shareholder loan. France does not impose a universal FX purpose-code system; banks use internal payment-purpose fields and may request a capital subscription agreement, loan agreement, board resolution, and accounting treatment. Verify beneficiary name and IBAN, intermediary-bank requirements, sanctions screening, foreign-investment-control exposure, tax consequences, and any applicable Banque de France balance-of-payments or statistical reporting. Do not use unexplained third-party remitters or cash funding.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for euro-area suppliers where appropriate, and SWIFT customer credit transfer for non-SEPA or foreign-currency settlements. MT103 is the traditional SWIFT customer-payment format; banks are migrating to ISO 20022 correspondent-payment messages, so the current bank-specific format must be confirmed. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit under UCP 600, with documentary presentation through the issuing, advising, confirming, and nominated banks. Require invoices, transport documents, insurance documents where applicable, packing lists, certificates of origin, customs data, sanctions and export-control checks, and segregation of duties. Reconcile each payment to an approved purchase order, invoice, shipment, and counterparty record. For open-account trade, establish counterparty limits, payment terms, dual approval, beneficiary-change call-back controls, and trade-document retention. Confirm that any bank guarantee, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or supply-chain-finance product is within the bank's mandate and supported by underlying commercial documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards for forecast or committed receivables and payables, subject to documented hedging purpose, counterparty approval, suitability assessment, ISDA or local master documentation, collateral terms where applicable, and compliance with EU derivatives rules.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies that are non-convertible or subject to local settlement restrictions, provided the product is legally available, the settlement index and fixing source are documented, the counterparty is properly authorized, and the SARL understands cash-settlement and basis risk.

FX swaps for short-term liquidity and currency-mismatch management, subject to documented maturities, counterparty limits, pricing controls, and applicable EMIR reporting, risk-mitigation, and clearing requirements.

Plain-vanilla FX options and collars for asymmetric protection, only after suitability, premium, valuation, accounting, and termination-risk review; complex or leveraged structures should be prohibited unless separately approved by the board and treasury policy.

EUR foreign-currency accounts, natural hedging through matching currency receipts and payments, and contractual currency clauses as non-derivative risk-management tools. Hedging must be linked to identifiable exposures, independently confirmed, periodically marked to market, and recorded under the applicable French accounting framework or adopted IFRS policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholders' Ordinary General Meeting approving annual financial statements (AGO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; prerequisite to registry and tax filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order may compel convocation; manager personally liable for losses; criminal fine of up to €9,000 for deliberate non-convocation; non-approval precludes timely deposit of accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and liasse fiscale (form 2065 plus financial schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) via electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of financial year-end; calendar-year entities file by early May (typically 3 May).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; late-filing increases of 5% (within 30 days), 10% (after 30 days) or 40% (after formal notice); persistent default exposes entity to enforced assessment and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements at the Commercial Court Registry (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce via INPI Guichet Unique; publication updated in the RCS file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; calendar-year companies habitually file by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry formal notice and judicial injunction under daily penalty (astreinte); repeated failure for successive years may trigger administrative strike-off from the Register of Commerce and Companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner register verification and update (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the registered office; changes filed with INPI/Greffe through Guichet Unique within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous register; filing update within 30 days of any share transfer or change in control; annual re-affirmation accompanies general meeting for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative and criminal sanctions for inaccurate or concealed beneficial ownership; manager may be disqualified; AML supervisors may impose fines separate from registry penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT regularization and intra-Community transaction statement (where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP (CA12 annual declaration for the simplified VAT scheme; monthly/quarterly returns if under normal scheme)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simplified scheme: CA12 due by 3 May of the following tax year. Normal scheme: no separate annual VAT form; monthly/quarterly returns remain due under the tax calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; omission can re-open the assessment period and trigger a 40% bad-faith or 80% abusive-act penalty in cases of deliberate concealment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when the SARL exceeds two of three thresholds at year-end: total balance sheet €4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax €8,000,000; average workforce 50 employees. Also compulsory for certain control relationships, public-interest entities, or where shareholders representing at least one-third of the capital request it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général / ANC regulation 2014-03) for individual statutory accounts; IFRS may be used only for consolidated financial statements and is not available for domestic SARL statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The register of beneficial owners must be kept permanently at the registered office. Any share transfer or change in ownership structure that affects direct or indirect control or the 25%-or-more ownership threshold must be reported to the registry within 30 days. At each ordinary general meeting, management must review and confirm that the UBO register is accurate and consistent with the annual share register; no separate French annual UBO declaration is imposed beyond this maintenance obligation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Share Transfers (registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of Directors (or, for SARL, register of managers/gérants)
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Managerial Decisions
Register of Beneficial Owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 25,000 per year depending on turnover and transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (CGI Art. 219-I-a for fiscal years commencing on/after 1 January 2022); reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% held directly by individuals.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Permanent reduced 15% bracket for eligible SMEs; Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (CIR) at 30% of qualifying R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million per year; Crédit d'Impôt Innovation (CII) at 20% of defined innovation expenditures capped at EUR 400,000 per year; scientific and technical cooperation agreements may yield additional credits; the CICE (competitiveness employment credit) was abolished for salaries paid after 31 December 2018, but crystallized balances remain usable; group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) permits offsetting profits against tax losses of 95%-owned French subsidiaries; SARL engaged in commercial re-invoicing trade is compulsorily subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés and cannot rely on the family SARL income-tax option.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Déclaration de Résultats) together with the 2050-series liasse fiscale (bilan 2050, compte de résultat 2051, annexe 2053, 2058-A/B), e-filed through the DGFiP GEFIP professional portal at impots.gouv.fr (obligatory electronic transmission for all corporate filers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (liquidation définitive de l'impôt sur les sociétés)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return must be filed by the second working day following 1 May; for any fiscal year ending other than 31 December, the return is due no later than the expiration of the third month following the fiscal year-end; the final balance of IS (solde) is payable on the same filing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result before loss carry-forward: accounting net income reduced by time-based add-backs (réintégrations) and deductions (déductions) including depreciation, provisions, and non-deductible expenses (e.g., art. 39-4 CGI fines, excessive intercompany charges).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident gérant must consolidate all French permanent-establishment results into this single French return; foreign-currency accounts must be converted at the year-end ECB rate; no foreign-loss deduction is admissible at this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carried-forward tax losses (déficits reportables) offset against current-year taxable profit, subject to the statutory annual cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses realized by the SARL itself may be imputed; a non-resident shareholder's foreign losses cannot be transferred into this box; retain the 2058-B schedule detailing the loss history.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits applied against the IS liability, including CIR, CII, foreign tax credits, and withholding tax credits arising on French-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are admitted only where a tax treaty or EU directive authorizes them; the taxpayer must append the Form 5000 residence certificate and source-income evidence before any reduction is accepted by the service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net long-term capital gains and losses realized during the year; gains are taxed at the long-term bracket (12.80% IS rate) while ordinary re-invoicing margins are included in the A-box result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a re-invoicing hub, ensure gains are not mischaracterized as French immovable property gains which fall outside the IS return; any disposal of substantial French real estate must be separately reported to the Property tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the beneficial owner(s) of the SARL and certification that the register of beneficial owners is up to date at the trade registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident individuals owning the SARL must provide verified identity documentation; failure to maintain the RBE can be treated as an administrative irregularity that blocks reduced dividend withholding and DTA application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late/non-filing: automatic 10% surcharge where the return is filed within 30 days after the deadline; 40% where the administration issues a formal notice (mise en demeure) and the default continues; 80% for abusive schemes or fraudulent maneuvers (CGI Art. 1728, Art. 1729-1730); late-payment interest at 0.20% per month (CGI Art. 1731); flat fine of EUR 150 for failure to e-file; EUR 15 per missing attachment; interest accrues from the filing deadline to full settlement.
